short_answer.question: Name the essential parts of human eye,
short_answer.model_answer: (a) Retina (6) Eye lens (c) Cornea (d) Pupil (e) Iris

short_answer.question: Which liquid fills the space behind the cornea?
short_answer.model_answer: Aqueous humour is filled in the space behind the cornea.

short_answer.question: Which part of the eye controls the amount of light entering the eye?
short_answer.model_answer: Pupil controls the amount of light entering the eye.

short_answer.question: What is eye lens made of ?
short_answer.model_answer: Eye lens is made of transparent and flexible jelly like material.

short_answer.question: How is the sense of vision carried from the eye to the brain?
short_answer.model_answer: Through optical nerve, sense of vision is carried from eye to the brain.

short_answer.question: Which liquid fills the space between eye lens and retina?
short_answer.model_answer: Vitreous humour.

short_answer.question: Why is blind spot so called?
short_answer.model_answer: An image formed at this point is not sent to brain.

short_answer.question: What is the number of receptors contained in the retina?
short_answer.model_answer: Retina contains more than 125 millions receptors which are of two types, rods and cones.

short_answer.question: What is meant by far point?
short_answer.model_answer: The farthest point upto which an normal human eye can see objects clearly is known as far point.

short_answer.question: Why can you not see an object clearly if it is placed very close to your eye?
short_answer.model_answer: CHAPTER 11 Human Eye and The Colorful World For a human eye, there is a near point, 25 cm. If the distance of the object is lesser than this distance, eye cannot see object clearly.

short_answer.question: When you enter from a bright sunshine into a dark room, you are not able to see clearly for sometime, why?
short_answer.model_answer: In bright light, pupil had become small.

short_answer.question: On what factor the colour of the scattered light depends?
short_answer.model_answer: The colour of the scattered light depends on the size of scattered particles.

short_answer.question: What is Presbyopia ?
short_answer.model_answer: Presbyopia is a kind of eye defect in old persons due to ageing. It happens due to decrease in flexibility of eye lens and weakening of ciliary muscles.

short_answer.question: What is twinkling of stars due to?
short_answer.model_answer: Twinkling of star is due to atmosphere refraction.

short_answer.question: Define dispersion of white light.
short_answer.model_answer: The splitting of white light into its constituents seven colours is called dispersion of light.

short_answer.question: What kind of lens is used in the spectacles of a person suffering from myopia (near sightedness)?
short_answer.model_answer: A diverging lens/concave lens is used for a person suffering from near sightedness/ myopia.

short_answer.question: Name the part of the human eye that helps in changing the focal length of the eye lens.
short_answer.model_answer: Ciliary muscles help in changing the focal length of the eye lens.

short_answer.question: Write the value of near point of distinct vision for normal eye.
short_answer.model_answer: For a normal human eye the value of near point of distinct vision is 25 cm.

short_answer.question: What is the range of vision for a normal human eye?
short_answer.model_answer: Range of vision is 25 cm to infinity.

short_answer.question: Name the two phenomena involved in the formation of rainbow.
short_answer.model_answer: The phenomena involved in formation of rainbow are dispersion and total internal reflection and refraction.

short_answer.question: Name the component of white light that deviates the least and the most while passing through a prism.
short_answer.model_answer: Red colour deviates the least and violet colour deviates the most.

short_answer.question: Name the part responsible for the power of accommodation of the eye.
short_answer.model_answer: Ciliary muscles help for the power accommodation of the eye.

short_answer.question: Name the condition resulting due to the eye lens becoming cloudy.
short_answer.model_answer: Cataract.

short_answer.question: Why sky appears dark to the passengers flying at high altitudes?
short_answer.model_answer: There is no atmosphere at high altitudes. Hence no scattered light can reach to the eye.

short_answer.question: A person suffering from an eye defect uses lenses of power – 1D. Name the defect he is suffering from and the nature of lens used.
short_answer.model_answer: He uses a concave lens (negative power) because he is suffering from myopia.

short_answer.question: Which colour of white light suffers (i) least deviation and (ii) maximum deviation when a beam of white light passes through a glass prism?
short_answer.model_answer: Longer wavelength light (red) suffers least deviation and shorter wavelength (violet) suffers maximum deviation when white light is passed through a prism.

short_answer.question: How can change of size of eyeball be one of the reason for: (a) Myopic (b) Hypermetropic Compare the size of eyeball with that of a normal eye in each case. How does this change of size affect the position of image in each case?
short_answer.model_answer: (a) The eye suffering from myopia, has long eye ball than that of normal eye due to which the retina is at a larger distance from the eye lens. This results in the formation of the image in front of the retina. (b) The eye suffering from hypermetropia has short eye ball than that of normal eye due to which the retina is smaller distance from the eye lens. This results in the formation of the image behind the retina.

short_answer.question: State the function of pupil and ciliary muscles.
short_answer.model_answer: a. Pupil controls the amount of light entering the eye. b. Ciliary muscles help in accommodation of power of eye lens.

short_answer.question: A child sitting in a classroom is not able to read clearly the writing on the blackboard. a. Name the type of defect from which his eye is suffering. b. With the help of a ray diagram show how this defect can be remedied.
short_answer.model_answer: a. Myopia b. Myopia can be remedied by using concave lens.

short_answer.question: What is meant by persistence of vision?
short_answer.model_answer: On removing object seen, its impression persists on the retina for 16 1 th second. The inability of human brain to perceive more than two images formed on the retina within interval of 16 1 th of a second is called persistence of vision. In this case, both the images merge and give a sensation of continuity.

short_answer.question: List four common defects of vision that can be corrected with the use of spectacles.
short_answer.model_answer: (i) Myopia (ii) Hypermetropia (iii) presbyopia (iv) Astigmatism.

short_answer.question: (a) Explain how a normal human eye is able to see distinctly the object placed at a distance as well as those placed at a nearer distance. (b) What is the far point and near point of a normal human eye?
short_answer.model_answer: (a) Ciliary muscles change the curvature of eye lens as per requirement of the eye. This changes the focal length of eye lens. When muscles are relaxed, lens becomes thin and distant objects are seen clearly. While seeing closer objects, muscles contract, this thickens the eye lens and focal length decreases. (b) Far point — Infinity. Near point — 25 cm from the eye.

short_answer.question: What is meant by least distance of distinct vision? How does this vary between the very young and old people?
short_answer.model_answer: Least distance of distinct vision is the minimum distance between eye and object to see it clearly. In young, the least distance of distinct vision is lesser and for old people it is more.

short_answer.question: Define dispersion of white light and name the colours of white light in order.
short_answer.model_answer: When white light is passed through a prism, it splits into its seven constituent colours. Splitting of white light into its constituent colours is called dispersion. Seven constituent colours are – violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red. (VIBGYOR).

short_answer.question: Describe an experiment to discuss the recombination of dispersed light.
short_answer.model_answer: If another identical prism is placed in inverted position in front of a prism then dispersed colours obtained from first prism get recombine to produce white light.

short_answer.question: Explain why do stars twinkle and planets do not?
short_answer.model_answer: The light coming from star get refracted through the atmospheric layers. Due to this, the star appear slightly higher than its actual position. Since the densities of atmospheric layers changes frequently and hence the position of the star appear changes continuously stars are very distant point-sized objects. As the path of rays of light coming from star is continuously changes. So sometimes light enters into our eyes and some times it faints. This is twinkling of the star. Since planets are closer to us, their size is also big. Our eyes receive light from different points of the planets. Hence planets do not twinkle.

short_answer.question: List two causes leading to myopia of the eye. Draw ray diagrams to show the image formation in case of defective eye and corrected eye.
short_answer.model_answer: Causes of Myopia a. Excessive curvature of cornea b. Elongation of eye ball.

short_answer.question: (a) What is the least distance of distinct vision for the normal eye? (b) Does the above distance increase or decrease for long sighted eye? Give reason for your answer with diagram.
short_answer.model_answer: (a) For a normal human eye, the least distance of distinct vision is 25 cm. (b) Least distance of distinct vision increases for long sighted eye. A hypermetropic eye can see upto infinite distance, which is more than 25 cm.

short_answer.question: Explain how a normal human eye is able to see distinctly the object placed at a distance as well as those placed at a nearer distance. What is the far point and near point of a normal human eye?
short_answer.model_answer: To see a near object, the focal length of the eye should be small and vice versa. The focal length of the eye lens can be adjusted by ciliary muscles. When one see near object, ciliary muscles decreases the focal length and for distant object, ciliary muscles increases the focal length. Far point — Infinity. Near point — 25 cm from the eye.

short_answer.question: An old person is unable to see clearly nearby object as well as distant objects, (i) What defect of vision is he suffering from? (ii) What kind of lens will be required to see clearly the nearby as well as distant objects? Give reason.
short_answer.model_answer: (i) Old person is suffering from presbyopia. (ii) He cannot see near objects as well as distant objects, so he has to use bifocal lenses which consists of concave and convex lenses both.

short_answer.question: Why does it take sometimes to see the objects in a dim room when we enter the room from bright sunlight outside?
short_answer.model_answer: In bright sunlight, pupil of eye contracts to control the light. When we enter a dim room, pupil takes some time to expand to allow more light to see the objects clearly.

short_answer.question: Why does the clear sky appear blue? How would the sky appear in the absence of earth’s atmosphere?
short_answer.model_answer: Scattering of light 1 4 \ l where l is the wavelength of light, i.e. least wavelength will scatter more and vice versa. Blue colour light has shorter wavelength and hence scattered more than other colours. In space, there is no atmosphere hence no scattering of light happens in the space so space appears black.

short_answer.question: Why do we observe difference in colours of the sun during sunrise, sunset and noon?
short_answer.model_answer: During the sunrise or sunset, the sun is at horizon. Most of the blue light and other light of shorter wavelength are scattered most. Only the longer wavelength (red) reaches to us. That’s why sun appears red during the sunrise or sunset. At noon, the Sun appears white because it is at our head and all wavelength reaches to us due to little of the blue and violet colours are scattered due to least distance travelled by fight.

short_answer.question: (a) Write the function of each of the following parts of human eye: (i) Cornea (ii) Iris (iii) Crystalline lens (iv) Ciliary muscles (b) Why does the sun appear reddish early in the morning? short_answer.model_answer: (a) Function of Human eye: (i) Cornea focuses light ray to enter the eye. (ii) Iris control and regulate amount of light entering the eye and control the size of pupil. (iii) Crystalline lens is like a convex lens which converge light rays on the retina. (iv) Ciliary muscles adjust focal length of eye lens by contraction and relaxation so that sharp image can be obtained on the retina. (b) During morning and evening time, sun is at the horizon, sunlight has to travel longer distance in atmosphere. Violet and blue colours etc. of shorter wavelength scatter in the space only. The longer wavelength red colour reaches to the observer on earth and sun appears reddish. No, because there is no atmosphere on moon and no scattering of light takes place there.

When sun is overhead at noon, sun rays travels smaller distance, due to little scattering of blue and violet colour wavelength almost all wavelengths reach to earth and due to this sun appears white.

short_answer.question: State the cause of dispersion, when white light enters a glass prism. Explain with a diagram.
short_answer.model_answer: When white light passes through a prism it splits into its constituent colours, because each coloured light has different speed in prism. Prism has different refractive index for these light rays and so deviates through different angles when emerge out from the prism. Deviation for violet colour (shortest wavelength) is most and for red colour (largest wavelength) deviation is least.

These droplets refract and disperse the incident sunlight, then reflect it internally and finally refract it again when it comes out of the rain drop. Due to distortion of sunlight and internally reflection, different colours reach to the observer.

short_answer.question: (a) What is dispersion of white light? What is the cause of such dispersion? Draw a diagram, to show the dispersion of white light by a glass prism. (b) A glass prism is able to produce a spectrum when white light passes through it but a glass slab does not produce any spectrum. Explain why it is so.
short_answer.model_answer: (a) Dispersion : When white light is passed through a prism it splits into its constituent colours splitting of white light into its constituent colours is known as dispersion. Light of all wavelengths in vacuum travel with the same speed but have the different speeds in a medium due to different refractive light of indices for them. As a result different wavelength, deviate at different angle. Red colour deviates least when as violet colour deviates most. (b) In glass slab also, dispersion takes place at AB surface, but these splitted colours emerge out in the form of a parallel beam which becomes white. A glass slab whose focus are parallel can be considered as comprising two prisms of same refractive angle. The second identical prism can be considered in an inverted position w.r.t. first prism. When a beam of white light passes from one prism it get dispersed, but on passing through the second inverted prism, the spectrum recombine to form a white light.

short_answer.question: (a) Explain the following terms used in relation to defects of vision and corrections provided for them: (i) Myopia (ii) Astigmatism (iii) Bifocal lenses (iv) Far sightedness. (b) Describe with a ray diagram how a person with myopia can be helped by spectacles.
short_answer.model_answer: (a) (i) Myopia is a kind of defect in human eye due to which a person can see near by objects clearly but unable to see the distant objects. Myopia is due to (i) excessive curvature of cornea (ii) elongation of eye ball. (ii) Astigmatism is a kind of human eye defect in which he cannot see simultaneously horizontal and vertical lines both. This defect arises either when the cornea or the eye lens or both are not perfectly spherical. It can be corrected by using cylindrical lenses. (iii) Bifocal lenses with the ageing a person may suffer myopia and hypermetropia. For correction of these defects he is advised to use bifocal lenses whose upper half is concave and lower part is convex to see distant and reading purposes respectively. (iv) Far sightedness, a person suffering from this defect can see distant objects but unable to see nearby objects clearly. The image of an objects is formed beyond the retina.
